User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user account within the PDF Spark application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

email.description: The user's email address, used for communication and account identification.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user account was created.

lastLoginAt.description: Timestamp indicating the user's last successful login.

subscriptionId.description: Reference to the current Subscription plan for this user. (Relationship: Subscription 1:N User)

Subscription.title: Subscription
Subscription.description: Defines different subscription plans and their associated features and limits.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Subscription entity.

name.description: The name of the subscription plan (e.g., 'Free', 'Premium').

description.description: A detailed description of the subscription plan's benefits and features.

price.description: The monetary price of the subscription plan (e.g., monthly or yearly cost).

currency.description: The currency in which the subscription price is denominated (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR').

dailyOperationLimit.description: The maximum number of operations a user on this plan can perform daily.

maxFileSizeMB.description: The maximum allowed size for a single file upload in megabytes (MB).

storageLimitGB.description: The total cloud storage limit for user files on this plan in gigabytes (GB).

features.description: A list of features included in this subscription plan.

File.title: File
File.description: Represents a document (PDF, DOCX, TXT, Image) uploaded by a user or generated by an operation.

id.description: Unique identifier for the File entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who owns or uploaded this file. (Relationship: User 1:N File)

originalFileName.description: The original name of the file as provided by the user during upload.

storagePath.description: The internal path or URL where the file is stored in cloud storage.

fileType.description: The MIME type of the file (e.g., 'application/pdf', 'image/jpeg', 'text/plain').

fileSize.description: The size of the file in bytes.

uploadedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the file was uploaded.

isProcessed.description: Indicates whether this file is the result of a processing operation.

associatedOperationId.description: Reference to the Operation that generated this file, if it is an output file. (Relationship: Operation 1:N File)

Operation.title: Operation
Operation.description: Represents a single action performed by a user using one of the PDF Spark tools (e.g., PDF Merge, AI Summarize).

id.description: Unique identifier for the Operation entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who initiated this operation. (Relationship: User 1:N Operation)

status.description: The current status of the operation (e.g., 'PENDING', 'PROCESSING', 'COMPLETED', 'FAILED').

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the operation was initiated.

completedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the operation was completed or failed.

inputFilesIds.description: An array of IDs referencing the File entities used as input for this operation. (Relationship: File N:N Operation)

outputFilesIds.description: An array of IDs referencing the File entities generated as output by this operation. (Relationship: File N:N Operation)

aiPrompt.description: The specific prompt text sent to the AI service for AI-based operations.

aiResult.description: A summary or snippet of the AI response, or a reference to a File ID if the AI output is a document.

UsageLog.title: UsageLog
UsageLog.description: Records individual tool usages or API requests made by users for analytics, rate limiting, and potential billing.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UsageLog entry.

userId.description: Reference to the User who made the request. (Relationship: User 1:N UsageLog)

operationId.description: Reference to the Operation entity associated with this usage log entry, if applicable. (Relationship: Operation 1:N UsageLog)

toolUsed.description: The specific tool or API endpoint accessed (e.g., 'PDF_MERGE_TOOL', 'AI_SUMMARIZE_API').

requestTimestamp.description: Timestamp indicating when the request was made.

costUnits.description: A numeric value representing the 'cost' or consumption units of the request for rate limiting or billing purposes.

ipAddress.description: The IP address from which the user's request originated, for security and rate limiting.

definition.description: Stores individual user profiles. Access is restricted to the owner matching `request.auth.uid`. Includes `id` field which corresponds to the Firebase Authentication UID.

Contains definitions of different subscription plans. These documents are primarily read-only for authenticated users and managed by the backend/administrators. No specific denormalized authorization fields are needed as access is global for plan details.

params.name: subscriptionId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific subscription plan.

definition.description: Stores metadata for files uploaded or generated by a user. Access is restricted to the user specified by `userId` in the path. Includes denormalized 'userId' field for authorization independence, ensuring ownership verification without parent document lookups.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns this file.

params.name: fileId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific file.

definition.description: Records details of operations performed by a user (e.g., PDF merge, AI summarize). Access is restricted to the user specified by `userId` in the path. Includes denormalized 'userId' field for authorization independence, crucial for atomic operation creation and rule evaluation.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who performed this operation.

params.name: operationId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific operation.

definition.description: Logs individual tool usages and API requests for rate limiting and auditing purposes. Access is restricted to the user specified by `userId` in the path. Includes denormalized 'userId' field for authorization independence, enabling direct rule checks for usage tracking.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user whose usage is being logged.

params.name: usageLogId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific usage log entry.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure prioritizes Authorization Independence and Structural Segregation to ensure robust, debuggable security rules and efficient data access. User-specific data is organized hierarchically under a `/users/{userId}` root, creating clear ownership and simplifying authorization. Each user's `File`, `Operation`, and `UsageLog` documents reside in subcollections: `/users/{userId}/files`, `/users/{userId}/operations`, and `/users/{userId}/usageLogs`, respectively. This path-based ownership (`request.auth.uid == userId`) makes security rules for these collections atomic and eliminates the need for `get()` operations, which would otherwise introduce complex authorization dependencies and break batch/transactional writes. For instance, when creating an operation or file, the `userId` in the path directly asserts ownership.

Crucially, for Authorization Independence, every document within these user-specific subcollections (e.g., `File`, `Operation`, `UsageLog`) also explicitly includes the `userId` field. This denormalization ensures that even if a document were accessed out of context (e.g., via an index), its ownership is immediately verifiable without traversing the path or performing additional reads. This adheres to the principle of denormalizing authorization context.

Structural Segregation is applied by ensuring each collection has a homogeneous security posture. The top-level `/users` collection holds individual user profiles. The `/subscriptions` collection, on the other hand, stores global, read-only definitions of subscription plans, accessible to all authenticated users for viewing, but writable only by administrators (a role not explicitly defined in Firestore here, but assumed via backend management). This clear separation prevents mixing data with different access requirements.

Regarding QAPs (Rules are not Filters), the structure supports secure `list` operations by design. For example, a query to `/users/{userId}/files` for a specific `userId` will inherently be secure because the Firestore rules can easily enforce that `request.auth.uid` matches the `{userId}` wildcard in the path. This means the client application can only ever 'list' files, operations, or usage logs that belong to the currently authenticated user, eliminating the risk of accidental data exposure through broad queries and moving the authorization burden from client-side filtering to robust server-side rules.
